'''John Edward Franz''' (December 21, 1929 – April 27, 2026) was an American [[Organic chemistry|organic chemist]] who discovered the [[herbicide]] [[glyphosate]] while working at [[Monsanto Company]] in 1970.<ref name=US3799758>[https://patents.google.com/patent/US3799758 US Patent 3,799,758]</ref> The chemical became the active ingredient in [[Roundup (herbicide)|Roundup]], a broad-spectrum, post-emergence herbicide. Franz earned acclaim and rewards for this breakthrough.{{Promotion inline|date=November 2023}} He also had over 840 patents to his name worldwide.

==Career==
Franz spent his entire career at Monsanto in [[St. Louis, Missouri]]. After finishing his Ph.D., Franz was hired by Monsanto as a Resident Chemist in 1955.<ref name=Lemelson>Lemelson-MIT Program.  [https://web.archive.org/web/20071208092208/http://web.mit.edu/invent/iow/franz.html Inventor of the Week: John Franz]</ref> He focused on process research, new [[polymer]] synthesis, and the development of [[Plasticizer|plasticizers]] and polymer [[Flame retardant|flame retardants]].<ref name=Scientist>Strong, Colby. [http://www.the-scientist.com/article/display/10101/ People: Monsanto Scientist John E. Franz Wins 1990 Perkins Medal for Applied Chemistry] The Scientist 10 (1990): 28</ref><ref name=MonsantoBio>Monsanto  [https://web.archive.org/web/20080724175539/http://www.monsanto.com/features/franz_bio.asp Biography of Dr. John Franz]</ref> Franz received two patents while working in the Organic Division, one for [[nitrates]] in 1960, and one for a fire retardant in 1967. He transferred to the Agricultural Division of Monsanto in 1967, motivated by the department's "emphasis on publishing, academic contacts, and the freedom to pursue ideas."<ref>{{Cite web |title=John E. Franz & the Glyphosate Discovery |url=https://www.no-tillfarmer.com/articles/11484-john-e-franz-and-the-glyphosate-discovery |access-date=2023-12-04 |website=www.no-tillfarmer.com |language=en}}</ref> Because his background was in [[organic chemistry]], Franz familiarized himself with the new field by spending a year studying and learning about plant physiology and biochemistry before beginning research.{{Citation needed|date=November 2023}}

He discovered the herbicide [[glyphosate]], and received five dollars for his first patent from Monsanto.<ref name=MonsantoBio/> From 1960 to 1988, he received over 840 patents worldwide, including approximately fifty in the United States. Over the course of his career, Franz published over forty papers and wrote the book ''Glyphosate: A Unique Global Herbicide'' with Michael K. Mao and James A. Sikorski. He was promoted to Senior Scientific Fellow in 1975, then Distinguished Fellow in 1980. Later in his career, he returned to the organic division to concentrate on environmentally friendly products until he retired in 1991.{{Citation needed|date=November 2023}}

===Discovery of glyphosate===
Researchers at Monsanto had been searching for an herbicide that was effective against [[Annual vs. perennial plant evolution|annual and perennial]] weeds for nine years but found little success.  They knew of two [[phosphonic acid]] compounds that were ineffective against weeds, and the researchers were not able to advance the compounds. Franz took over the research in 1969 and incorrectly hypothesized that the [[phosphonic acids]] acted as proherbicides that were metabolized to active compounds rather than herbicides. Franz and his research team screened possible metabolites and synthesized compounds and eventually discovered [[glyphosate]] in 1970.<ref name=Lemelson/>

Although all of the patents regarding glyphosate list Franz as the sole inventor and the Monsanto Company as the assignee, Franz acknowledged that the discovery was a group effort. In 2007, when he was inducted into the [[National Inventor's Hall of Fame]], Franz said, "It's a recognition of the entire team of scientists who worked on and supported the development of Roundup herbicides".<ref>Monsanto Press Release February 9, 2007 [http://news.monsanto.com/press-release/inventor-roundup-be-inducted-national-inventors-hall-fame Inventor of Roundup To Be Inducted Into National Inventors Hall of Fame]</ref> [[Glyphosate]] works by absorption through leaves, and then moving rapidly to a plant's roots, rhizomes, and meristems. This breakthrough spurred Monsanto to design and produce [[Roundup Ready|plants genetically immune to glyphosates]] in order to make it easier for farmers to thoroughly spray down their fields for weeds without killing their own crops.<ref name=C&ENews/>

Once glyphosate was invented, it took four years to reach the market. It was first introduced as "Roundup", and is still best known by that brand.<ref name=Lemelson/>

Glyphosate has been called by experts in herbicides "virtually ideal" due to its broad spectrum and low toxicity compared with other herbicides.<ref name=C&ENews>[http://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/cen-v068n011.p029 Monsanto's John E. Franz Wins 1990 Perkin Medal]  Chem. Eng. News, 1990, 68 (11), pp 29–30  DOI: 10.1021/cen-v068n011.p029</ref><ref>Stephen O Duke and Stephen B. Powles (2008) [http://naldc.nal.usda.gov/download/17918/PDF Glyphosate: a once-in-a-century herbicide: Mini-review.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702211642/https://naldc.nal.usda.gov/download/17918/PDF |date=2019-07-02 }} Pest Management Science Pest Manag Sci 64:319–325</ref><ref>Pesticide Action Network UK.[http://www.pan-uk.org/pestnews/Actives/glyphosa.htm Glyphosate fact sheet] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160823030140/http://www.pan-uk.org/pestnews/Actives/glyphosa.htm |date=2016-08-23 }} Pesticides News No.33, September 1996, p28-29  PAN-UK says it is "a welcome move away from chemicals which are highly toxic to humans and other non target organisms, and from chemicals which cause direct and lasting damage to the environment" and of course cautions against overuse.</ref> However, the chemical’s use has come under attack in numerous countries, with bans or partial bans enacted, and thousands of lawsuits filed alleging the chemical is carcinogenic. German Chancellor [[Angela Merkel]] stated in June 2019 that “we will come to a point where glyphosate isn’t used anymore.”<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/austrian-herbicide-ban-adds-to-problems-for-roundup-owner-bayer-11562087770|title = Austrian Herbicide Ban Adds to Problems for Roundup Owner Bayer|newspaper = Wall Street Journal|date = 2 July 2019|last1 = Bender|first1 = Ruth}}</ref> [[Bayer]], which acquired Monsanto, stopped selling Roundup for residential use in 2023<ref>{{Cite web |title=Roundup Lawsuit Update December 2023 – Forbes Advisor |url=https://www.forbes.com/advisor/legal/product-liability/roundup-lawsuit-update/ |access-date=2023-12-04 |website=www.forbes.com|date=18 August 2022 }}</ref> "exclusively to manage litigation risk and not because of any safety concerns".<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=Five-Point Plan to Close the Roundup™ Litigation |url=https://www.bayer.com/en/roundup-litigation-five-point-plan |website=Bayer}}</ref> 

===Other research===
Franz undertook research in many areas during his time at Monsanto. Some of his other chemistry research includes antiauxin chemistry (isothiazoles, isoxazoles, pyrazoles), plant chemistry, [[cell membrane]] chemistry (glyceride and phospholipid syntheses, liposomes), plant hormone chemistry (abscissic acid analogs, ethylene generators), and nitride sulfide chemistry. He also performed research pertaining to reaction mechanisms, [[coenzyme A]] [[antimetabolite]]s, biorational design of herbicides, and periselective addition reactions of one- and threedipoles, as well as fundamental organic research.<ref name=Scientist/>

==Death==
Franz died on April 27, 2026, at the age of 96.<ref>{{cite web |title=John Edward Franz |url=https://www.luptonchapel.com/obituaries/John-Edward-Franz?obId=48236617 |website=Lupton-Millard Chapel |access-date=29 April 2026}}</ref>

==Honors==
Franz received awards for his discovery. In 1977, he was awarded the IR-100 award by Industrial Research magazine. In 1981, he received the first J.F. Queeny Award from Monsanto to honor an invention that was also a commercial success. He was the recipient of the 1987 [[National Medal of Technology]], one of the few agricultural technologies to ever receive the honor. Franz received the [[American Chemical Society]]’s [[Carothers Award]] in 1989 for "outstanding contributions and advances in industrial applications of chemistry". In 1990, he was awarded the [[Perkin Medal]] by the American Section of the [[Society of Chemical Industry]], based on his contributions to the research and development of applied chemistry. Franz also won the Outstanding Achievement Award in 1988, the 1988 Missouri Award, and was named the St. Louis Metropolitan Bar Association Inventor of the Year in 1986. Roundup was named one of the "Top 10 Products That Changed the Face of Agriculture" by the magazine Farm Chemicals in 1994. Franz was inducted into the United States' Inventor's Hall of Fame on May 5, 2007.<ref name="Lemelson" /><ref name="OH">{{cite web|author=Center for Oral History| title= John E. Franz |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/oral-histories/franz-john-e|website= [[Science History Institute]] }}</ref><ref name="transcript">{{cite book |first1=James J. |last1=Bohning |title=John E. Franz, Transcript of an Interview Conducted by James J. Bohning at St. Louis, Missouri on 29 November 1994 |date=29 November 1994 |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/sites/default/files/franz_je_0119_suppl.pdf |place=Philadelphia, PA |publisher=[[Science History Institute|Chemical Heritage Foundation]] |access-date=1 March 2018 |archive-date=2 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302103929/https://oh.sciencehistory.org/sites/default/files/franz_je_0119_suppl.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Monsanto has also created two awards in his honor. On December 8, 1995, the agricultural company introduced the Franz Sustainability Award, which consists of an annual $100,000 prize given to the individual or team that submits the best environmental project for improvement in the areas of conservation, technology, and/or education.<ref>Monsanto Press Release.  December 8, 1995 [http://www.thefreelibrary.com/MONSANTO+ANNOUNCES+JOHN+FRANZ+SUSTAINABILITY+AWARD-a017829020 Monsanto Announces John Franz Sustainability Award]</ref> Soon after Franz's induction into the Inventors' Hall of Fame in 2007, Monsanto announced a new annual scholarship called the Franz Innovation Award Scholarship. This scholarship is awarded each year to a graduate student taking organic chemistry at the [[University of Minnesota]].<ref>Monsanto Press Release. October 11, 2007. [http://news.monsanto.com/press-release/monsanto-announces-franz-innovation-award-scholarship Monsanto Announces Franz Innovation Award Scholarship] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007121731/http://news.monsanto.com/press-release/monsanto-announces-franz-innovation-award-scholarship |date=2017-10-07 }}</ref>

==Patents==
Franz had over 840 patents to his name concerning glyphosate and lesser known discoveries. Because of the nature of glyphosate, it requires many patents concerning identification, synthesis, and other processes required to produce the chemical.<ref>National Inventors Hall of Fame. [https://web.archive.org/web/20131005150930/http://www.invent.org/hall_of_fame/333.html Inventor Profile: John E. Franz]</ref>

His patents include:<ref>[http://patft.uspto.gov/netacgi/nph-Parser?Sect1=PTO2&Sect2=HITOFF&p=1&u=%2Fnetahtml%2FPTO%2Fsearch-adv.htm&r=0&f=S&l=50&d=PTXT&Query=IN%2F%22Franz%2C+John+E.%22 Patent Database Search Results: "John E. Franz" in U.S. Patent Collection]. U.S. Patent Database</ref>

* Patent Number: 3799758, Phytotoxicant compositions<ref name=US3799758 />
* Patent Number: 3853530, Regulating plants with n-phosphonomethylglycine and derivatives thereof<ref>[https://patents.google.com/patent/US3853530 US3853530]</ref>
* Patent Number: 3977860, Herbicidal compositions and methods employing esters of<ref>[https://patents.google.com/patent/US3977860 US3977860]</ref>
* Patent Number: 3954848, Process for producing N-phosphonomethy glycine<ref>[https://patents.google.com/patent/US3954848 US3954848]</ref>
* Patent Number: 4735649, Gametocides<ref>[https://patents.google.com/patent/US4735649 US4735649]</ref>
* Patent Number: 4634788, Herbicidal glyphosate oxime derivatives<ref>[https://patents.google.com/patent/US4634788 US4634788]</ref>
